The ACA's structural failures are the real issue—not expiring subsidies. For years, D.C. propped up Obamacare with temporary fixes while ignoring systemic fraud and Big Pharma's grip on pricing. Medicaid loses $55B annually to improper payments, yet bureaucrats blame coverage gaps on subsidy cliffs.

The solution isn't more taxpayer-funded bandaids—it's market-driven reforms that break hospital monopolies, expose pharmacy benefit manager kickbacks, and enforce Medicaid eligibility checks. South Texans deserve transparency, not a healthcare system rigged to funnel cash to middlemen while families get stuck with rising premiums.

Real affordability starts with auditing the $150B wasted annually on medical billing scams and hospital admin bloat—not perpetuating a broken subsidy model.
